title: Temurah 22
description: The end of the mishna on sin offerings left to die, Reish Lakish’s sin offering past its first year and Rava’s “two flaws”, an offering lost at night, what counts as lost, Rav Pappa’s blood in the cup, and a mishna on sin offerings and money that were lost, replaced and then found.
topics: 🔢 Why the mishna splits the five sin offerings into three and two
🪦 Reish Lakish: a sin offering past its first year is viewed as standing in a cemetery, and grazes
⚖️ Rabba’s temporary blemish and Rava’s two flaws, lost and unfit
🌙 Rava: an offering lost at night is not called lost; the rejected are not like the lost
🚪 What is lost? Mixed into a flock, behind the door, unknown to owner or shepherd
🥣 Rav Pappa: found while the replacement’s blood is in the cup, or one of two cups lost
💰 Mishna: money and animals lost, replaced and found; Rabbi and the Rabbis
🌊 First clause like the Rabbis, money clause like Rabbi?

a1.he: לֹא נֶהֱנִין וְלֹא מוֹעֲלִין, וְאִם עַד שֶׁלֹּא כִּיפְּרוּ הַבְּעָלִים — תִּרְעֶה עַד שֶׁתִּסְתָּאֵב, וְתִמָּכֵר וְיָבִיא בְּדָמֶיהָ אַחֶרֶת, וְעוֹשָׂה תְּמוּרָה וּמוֹעֲלִין בָּהּ.

a2.he: גְּמָ׳ מַאי טַעְמָא לָא תָּנֵי לְהוּ גַּבֵּי הֲדָדֵי? רֵישָׁא — פְּסִיקָא לֵיהּ, וְסֵיפָא — לָא פְּסִיקָא לֵיהּ.

a3.he: לְמָה לִי לְמִיתְנְיַיהּ גַּבֵּי מְעִילָה, לְמָה לִי לְמִיתְנְיַיהּ גַּבֵּי תְּמוּרָה? תְּנָא הָכָא תְּמוּרָה, וְאַיְּידֵי דִּתְנָא תְּמוּרָה — תְּנָא נָמֵי מְעִילָה, וְאַיְּידֵי דִּתְנָא גַּבֵּי מְעִילָה מְעִילָה — תְּנָא נָמֵי תְּמוּרָה.

a4.he: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: חַטָּאת שֶׁעִיבְּרָה שְׁנָתָהּ, רוֹאִין אוֹתָהּ כְּאִילּוּ עוֹמֶדֶת בְּבֵית הַקְּבָרוֹת, וְרוֹעָה.

a5.he: תְּנַן: שֶׁעִיבְּרָה שְׁנָתָהּ, וְאָבְדָה וְנִמְצֵאת בַּעֲלַת מוּם, אִם אַחַר שֶׁכִּיפְּרוּ בְּעָלִים — מֵתָה, תְּיוּבְתָּא דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ!

a6.he: אָמַר לָךְ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: כִּי קָתָנֵי רֵישָׁא ״מֵתָה״ — אַאָבְדָה וְנִמְצֵאת בַּעֲלַת מוּם, אִם אַחַר שֶׁכִּיפְּרוּ בְּעָלִים — תָּמוּת.

a7.he: אִי הָכִי, אֵימָא סֵיפָא: ״אִם עַד שֶׁלֹּא כִּיפְּרוּ הַבְּעָלִים תִּרְעֶה עַד שֶׁתִּסְתָּאֵב״, וְאִי בַּעֲלַת מוּם — הָא מְסָאֲבָא וְקַיְימָא!

a8.he: אָמַר רַבָּה: הָכִי קָאָמַר תַּנָּא: שֶׁאָבְדָה וְנִמְצֵאת בַּעֲלַת מוּם עוֹבֵר, אִם אַחַר שֶׁכִּפְּרוּ בְּעָלִים — מֵתָה, אִם קוֹדֶם שֶׁכִּיפְּרוּ בְּעָלִים — תִּרְעֶה עַד שֶׁתִּסְתָּאֵב בְּמוּם קָבוּעַ, וְתִימָּכֵר.

a9.he: אָמַר רָבָא: שְׁתֵּי תְּשׁוּבוֹת בַּדָּבָר, חֲדָא — דְּאִם כֵּן, ״יִשְׁמוֹר״ מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְמִיתְנֵי, וְעוֹד — ״שֶׁעִיבְּרָה שְׁנָתָהּ״ לְמַאי הִלְכְתָא קָתָנֵי?

a10.he: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: הָכִי קָתָנֵי, עִבְּרָה שְׁנָתָהּ וְאָבְדָה, אוֹ אָבְדָה וְנִמְצֵאת בַּעֲלַת מוּם — אַחַר שֶׁכִּיפְּרוּ הַבְּעָלִים מֵתָה, קוֹדֶם שֶׁכִּיפְּרוּ הַבְּעָלִים תִּרְעֶה עַד שֶׁתִּסְתָּאֵב וְתִימָּכֵר.

a11.he: וְצָרִיךְ לְמִיתְנֵי ״אִם אָבְדָה״ גַּבֵּי בַּעֲלַת מוּם, וְגַבֵּי עִבְּרָה שְׁנָתָהּ, דְּאִי תְּנָא גַּבֵּי שֶׁעִיבְּרָה שְׁנָתָהּ — הֲוָה אָמֵינָא הָתָם הוּא דְּמַהְנְיָא לַהּ אֲבֵדָה, מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא חַזְיָא לְמִילְּתַהּ, אֲבָל בַּעֲלַת מוּם דְּאִי לָא מוּמָא חַזְיָא — אֵימָא לָא תַּהֲנֵי לֵיהּ אֲבֵדָה.

a12.he: וְאִי תָּנֵי גַּבֵּי בַּעֲלַת מוּם, הָתָם הוּא דְּמַהְנְיָא לַהּ אֲבֵדָה, מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא חַזְיָא לְהַקְרָבָה, אֲבָל עִיבְּרָה שְׁנָתָהּ דְּחַזְיָא לְהַקְרָבָה, אֵימָא לָא תַּהֲנֵי לַהּ אֲבֵדָה, צְרִיכָא.

a13.he: וּמִי אָמַר רָבָא הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רָבָא: אֲבֵידָה דְּלַיְלָה לָא שְׁמַהּ אֲבֵידָה!

a14.he: לָא דָּמֵי אֲבֵידָה דְּלֵילְיָא — לָא חַזְיָא לָא לְגוּפַהּ וְלָא לִדְמֵי, אֲבָל הָא — נְהִי דִּלְגוּפַהּ לָא חַזְיָא, לִדְמֵי חַזְיָא.

a15.he: תְּנַן: הַשֵּׁנִי יִרְעֶה עַד שֶׁיִּסְתָּאֵב, וְיִמָּכֵר, וְיִפְּלוּ דָּמָיו לִנְדָבָה, לְפִי שֶׁאֵין חַטַּאת הַצִּיבּוּר מֵתָה. הָא דְּיָחִיד — מֵתָה!

a16.he: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים נִדְחִין, וּכְשֶׁהוּא מִתְכַּפֵּר — בְּשֵׁנִי שֶׁבְּזוּג שֵׁנִי מִתְכַּפֵּר.

a17.he: וְאִידַּךְ, קַמָּא, הָוֵה לֵיהּ כִּי עִיבְּרָה שְׁנָתָהּ, וְטַעְמָא דְּצִיבּוּר, הָא דְּיָחִיד — מֵתָה!

a18.he: אָמַר לָךְ: דְּחוּיִין לְחוּד, וַאֲבוּדִין לְחוּד. מַאי טַעְמָא? אֲבוּדִין — דַּעְתֵּיהּ עֲלֵיהוֹן, דִּילְמָא מִשְׁתַּכְחִין. דְּחוּיִין — לָא הָדָרִי מִתְחֲזַיִין.

b1.he: גּוּפָא: אָמַר רָבָא: אֲבוּדָה דְּלַיְלָה לָא שְׁמַהּ אֲבוּדָה. אַלִּיבָּא דְּמַאן? אִילֵימָא אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבָּנַן — מַאי אִירְיָא אֲבוּדָה דְּלַיְלָה? אֲפִילּוּ אֲבוּדָה דְּיוֹם נָמֵי, דְּאָמְרִי רַבָּנַן: אֲבוּדָה בִּשְׁעַת הַפְרָשָׁה רוֹעָה.

b2.he: וְאֶלָּא, אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי, עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלָּא אֲבֵידָה דְּיוֹם, אֲבָל אֲבֵידָה דְּלַיְלָה — אֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי מוֹדֶה דְּלִרְעִיָּיה אָזְלָא.

b3.he: אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: לְעוֹלָם אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבָּנַן, וְהָכָא בְמַאי עָסְקִינַן — בְּאָבְדָה בִּשְׁעַת כַּפָּרָה. עַד כָּאן לָא קָאָמְרִי רַבָּנַן אָבְדָה בִּשְׁעַת כַּפָּרָה מֵתָה, אֶלָּא הֵיכָא דְּעִיקַּר אֲבֵידָתָהּ בַּיּוֹם, אֲבָל הֵיכָא דְּעִיקַּר אֲבֵידָתָהּ בַּלַּיְלָה — לָא.

b4.he: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: נָקְטִינַן, אֲבֵידָה וְלֹא גְּנוּבָה, אֲבֵידָה וְלֹא גְּזוּלָה.

b5.he: הֵיכִי דָמֵי אֲבֵידָה? אָמַר רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא: אֲפִילּוּ אַחַת בְּעֶדְרוֹ, וַאֲפִילּוּ אַחַת בְּאַחַת. וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֲחוֹרֵי הַדֶּלֶת.

b6.he: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: הֵיכִי קָאָמַר? אֲחוֹרֵי הַדֶּלֶת הוּא דְּלֵיכָּא דְּקָא חָזֵי לַהּ, אֲבָל אַבָּרַאי דְּאִיכָּא דַּחֲזֵי לַהּ — לָא הָוְיָא אֲבוּדָה, אוֹ דִילְמָא אֲחוֹרֵי הַדֶּלֶת דְּאִי מַהְדַּר אַפֵּיהּ חָזֵי לַהּ — הָוְיָא אֲבוּדָה, וְכׇל שֶׁכֵּן אַבָּרַאי דְּלָא קָחָזֵי לַהּ? תֵּיקוּ.

b7.he: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: גָּמְרִינַן אֲבוּדָה מִמֶּנּוּ וְלֹא מֵרוֹעָהּ — לָא הָוְיָא אֲבוּדָה, וְכׇל שֶׁכֵּן אֲבוּדָה מֵרוֹעָהּ וְלֹא אֲבוּדָה מִמֶּנּוּ. אֲבוּדָה מִמֶּנּוּ וּמֵרוֹעָהּ, וְאֶחָד בְּסוֹף הָעוֹלָם מַכִּיר בָּהּ — מַאי? תֵּיקוּ.

b8.he: בָּעֵי רַב פָּפָּא: אֲבוּדָה בַּכּוֹס מַהוּ? אַלִּיבָּא דְּמַאן? אִילֵימָא אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי — הָאָמַר אֲבוּדָה בִּשְׁעַת הַפְרָשָׁה מֵתָה!

b9.he: אֶלָּא, כִּי קָמִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבָּנַן, מִי אָמְרִינַן: כִּי אָמְרִי רַבָּנַן בִּשְׁעַת הַפְרָשָׁה רוֹעָה, קוֹדֶם שֶׁיְּקַבֵּל דָּמָהּ בַּכּוֹס, אֲבָל הָכָא סְבִירָא לְהוּ: כָּל הָעוֹמֵד לִיזָּרֵק כְּזָרוּק דָּמֵי.

b10.he: אוֹ דִלְמָא, כְּמָה דְּלָא אִזְדְּרִיק דָּם — כִּי אָבְדָה בִּשְׁעַת הַפְרָשָׁה דָּמְיָא, וְרָעֲיָא.

b11.he: וְאִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי: לְעוֹלָם אַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי, כִּי קָמִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ — כְּגוֹן שֶׁקִּיבֵּל דָּמָהּ בִּשְׁתֵּי כוֹסוֹת, וְאָבַד אֶחָד מֵהֶן.

b12.he: וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּמַאן דְּאָמַר כּוֹס עוֹשֶׂה חֲבֵירוֹ דָּחוּי — לָא תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ, כִּי תִּיבְּעֵי לָךְ אַלִּיבָּא דְּמַאן דְּאָמַר כּוֹס עוֹשֶׂה חֲבֵירוֹ שִׁירַיִים.

b13.he: הָנֵי מִילֵּי — הֵיכָא דְּאִיתַנְהוּ לְתַרְוַיְיהוּ, דְּכֹל הֵיכָא דְּבָעֵי זָרֵיק; אֲבָל הָכָא — הָא לֵיכָּא, אוֹ דִלְמָא לָא שְׁנָא? תֵּיקוּ.

b14.he: מַתְנִי׳ הַמַּפְרִישׁ חַטָּאת, וְאָבְדָה, וְהִפְרִישׁ אַחֶרֶת תַּחְתֶּיהָ, וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִמְצֵאת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה — תָּמוּת.

b15.he: הַמַּפְרִישׁ מָעוֹת לְחַטָּאתוֹ, וְאָבְדוּ, וְהִפְרִישׁ חַטָּאת תַּחְתֵּיהֶם, וְאַחַר כָּךְ נִמְצְאוּ הַמָּעוֹת — יוֹלִיכֵם לְיָם הַמֶּלַח.

b16.he: הַמַּפְרִישׁ מָעוֹת לְחַטָּאת, וְאָבְדוּ, וְהִפְרִישׁ מָעוֹת אֲחֵרוֹת תַּחְתֵּיהֶן, וְלֹא הִסְפִּיק לִיקַּח חַטָּאת מֵהֶן עַד שֶׁנִּמְצְאוּ הָרִאשׁוֹנוֹת — יָבִיא מֵאֵלּוּ וּמֵאֵלּוּ חַטָּאת, וְהַשְּׁאָר יִפְּלוּ לִנְדָבָה.

b17.he: הַמַּפְרִישׁ מָעוֹת לְחַטָּאתוֹ וְאָבְדוּ, וְהִפְרִישׁ חַטָּאת תַּחְתֵּיהֶן, לֹא הִסְפִּיק לְהַקְרִיבָהּ עַד שֶׁנִּמְצְאוּ הַמָּעוֹת, וַהֲרֵי חַטָּאת בַּעַל מוּם — תִּמָּכֵר, וְיָבִיא מֵאֵלּוּ וּמֵאֵלּוּ חַטָּאת, וְהַשְּׁאָר יִפְּלוּ לִנְדָבָה.

b18.he: הַמַּפְרִישׁ חַטָּאת וְאָבְדָה, וְהִפְרִישׁ מָעוֹת תַּחְתֶּיהָ, וְלֹא הִסְפִּיק לִיקַּח מֵהֶן חַטָּאת עַד שֶׁנִּמְצָא חַטָּאתוֹ, וַהֲרֵי הִיא בַּעֲלַת מוּם — תִּימָּכֵר, וְיָבִיא מֵאֵלּוּ וּמֵאֵלּוּ חַטָּאת, וְהַשְּׁאָר יִפְּלוּ לִנְדָבָה.

b19.he: הַמַּפְרִישׁ חַטָּאתוֹ וְאָבְדָה, וְהִפְרִישׁ אַחֶרֶת תַּחְתֶּיהָ, לֹא הִסְפִּיק לְהַקְרִיבָהּ עַד שֶׁנִּמְצֵאת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה, וַהֲרֵי שְׁתֵּיהֶן בַּעֲלַת מוּם — יִמָּכְרוּ, וְיָבִיא מֵאֵלּוּ וּמֵאֵלּוּ חַטָּאת, וְהַשְּׁאָר יִפְּלוּ לִנְדָבָה.

b20.he: הַמַּפְרִישׁ חַטָּאת, וְאָבְדָה, וְהִפְרִישׁ אַחֶרֶת תַּחְתֶּיהָ, לֹא הִסְפִּיק לְהַקְרִיבָהּ עַד שֶׁנִּמְצֵאת הָרִאשׁוֹנָה, הָיוּ שְׁתֵּיהֶן תְּמִימוֹת — אַחַת מֵהֶן תִּיקְרַב חַטָּאת, וְהַשְּׁנִיָּה תָּמוּת, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי. וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֵין חַטָּאת מֵתָה אֶלָּא שֶׁנִּמְצֵאת מֵאַחַר שֶׁכִּיפְּרוּ הַבְּעָלִים, וְאֵין הַמָּעוֹת הוֹלְכִים לְיָם הַמֶּלַח אֶלָּא שֶׁנִּמְצְאוּ מֵאַחַר שֶׁכִּיפְּרוּ הַבְּעָלִים.

b21.he: הַמַּפְרִישׁ חַטָּאת, וַהֲרֵי הִיא בַּעֲלַת מוּם — מוֹכְרָהּ, וְיָבִיא בְּדָמֶיהָ אַחֶרֶת. רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: אִם קָרְבָה שְׁנִיָּה עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִשְׁחֲטָה — תָּמוּת, שֶׁכְּבָר כִּיפְּרוּ הַבְּעָלִים.

b22.he: גְּמָ׳ טַעְמָא דְּהִקְרִיב אַחֶרֶת תַּחְתֶּיהָ, הָא לֹא הִקְרִיב אַחֶרֶת תַּחְתֶּיהָ — רוֹעָה. מַנִּי? רַבָּנַן הִיא, דְּאָמְרִי: אֲבוּדָה בִּשְׁעַת הַפְרָשָׁה — רוֹעָה.

b23.he: אֵימָא סֵיפָא: הַמַּפְרִישׁ מָעוֹת לְחַטָּאת וְאָבְדוּ וְהִפְרִישׁ אֲחֵרִים תַּחְתֵּיהֶם — יָבִיא מֵאֵלּוּ וּמֵאֵלּוּ, וְהַשְּׁאָר יִפְּלוּ לִנְדָבָה. טַעְמָא מֵאֵלּוּ וּמֵאֵלּוּ, הָא הֵבִיא מֵאֶחָד מֵהֶן — הַשֵּׁנִי יוֹלִיכוֹ לְיָם הַמֶּלַח. אֲתָאן לְרַבִּי, דְּאָמַר: אֲבוּדָה בִּשְׁעַת הַפְרָשָׁה מֵתָה.

b24.he: רֵישָׁא רַבָּנַן, וְסֵיפָא רַבִּי?! הָנִיחָא לְרַב הוּנָא, דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא אָמַר רַב:

messages.text: Continued from 21b: chapter 4, ולד חטאת · Vlad Ḥatat, opened with a mishna. The offspring of a sin offering, the substitute for a sin offering and a sin offering whose owner has died are left to die; a sin offering whose first year has passed, or one lost and found blemished, if after the owner achieved atonement, shall die and does not render a substitute. The mishna continues:
Mishna

Furthermore, one may not derive benefit from any of these sin offerings ab initio, but if one derived benefit from them, after the fact, he is not liable to bring a sin offering for misuse of consecrated items.

notes.he: מדרבנן:
notes.en: One may not derive benefit: by rabbinic law.

notes.he: דאם נהנו פטורין מקרבן מעילה דכיון דלא היא ולא דמיה קריבין אזלא קדושתה:
notes.en: And one is not liable for misuse: if they derived benefit, they are exempt from the offering for misuse, for since neither it nor its value is sacrificed, its sanctity is gone.

notes.he: לא נהנין בה מדרבנן:
notes.en: One may not derive benefit from it: by rabbinic law.

notes.he: בה מדאורייתא:
notes.en: And one is not liable for misuse of it: by Torah law.

messages.text: And if the lost animal was found and discovered to be unfit before the owner achieved atonement for his sin with a different animal, it shall graze until it becomes blemished, and then it shall be sold. And he must bring another sin offering with the money received from the sale.

notes.he: אתרוייהו קאי כלומר כל זמן שלא כפרו הבעלים שלא רצה להתכפר באחרת:
notes.en: And if before the owner achieved atonement: this refers to both of them; that is, so long as the owner has not achieved atonement, [i.e.] he did not want to achieve atonement with another.

notes.he: ואעיברה שנתה קאי ולא אאותה שאבדה ונמצאת בעלת מום דהא מסאבא וקיימא ותימכר מיד ויביא בדמיה אחרת:
notes.en: It shall graze until it becomes blemished, etc.: this refers to the one whose year has passed, and not to the one that was lost and found blemished, for that one already stands blemished; it is sold at once, and he brings another with its money.

notes.he: אעברה שנתה דוקא קאי דאי אאבדה ונמצאת בעלת מום הא מסאבא וקיימא:
notes.en: It shall graze until it becomes blemished: this refers specifically to the one whose year has passed, for if it referred to the one lost and found blemished, it already stands blemished.

notes.he: אם עד שלא כפרו הבעלי' עיברה שנתה או נמצא ורוצין להתכפר בדמיהן אותה שעיברה שנתה תרעה ותימכר ואותה שהיא בעלת מום תימכר לאלתר ועושין תמורה כיון דיש בה קדושת דמים ומועלין בה נמי:
notes.en: If before the owner achieved atonement: [if] its year has passed, or it was found, and they want to achieve atonement with their value: the one whose year has passed shall graze and be sold, and the one that is blemished is sold at once. And they render a substitute, since they have sanctity of value, and one is liable for misuse of them too.

messages.text: And this animal renders a non-sacred animal exchanged for it a substitute, and one who derives benefit from this animal is liable for misusing it.

notes.he: הואיל ודמים מתירין ליקרב דהכי אמרינן בפרקין דלעיל (תמורה דף כ.) דדבר הרועה להסתאב עושה תמורה:
notes.en: And it renders a substitute: since its value is fit to be sacrificed, for so we said in the previous chapter (Temurah 20a), that something that grazes until it becomes blemished renders a substitute.

messages.text: Gemara

Although there are five types of sin offerings that are sequestered and left to die, the mishna initially states: The offspring of a sin offering, and the substitute for a sin offering, and a sin offering whose owner has died shall be sequestered and left to die, and only then mentions the remaining two types, a sin offering that is more than one year old and a sin offering that was lost and then found after the owner achieved atonement through the sacrifice of another animal. What is the reason the mishna does not teach them all together?

notes.dh: גמ' מאי טעמא לא תני להו כולהו בהדי הדדי
notes.he: אלא פליגי לה כלומר מאי שנא דתני לה בתרי בבי ולא תנא כולהו ה' חטאות ביחד אלא מפסיק בין ג' קמאי וב' בתראי:
notes.en: Gemara. What is the reason it does not teach them all together, [but divides them]: that is, why does it teach it in two clauses, and not teach all five sin offerings together, but instead separates the first three from the last two?

notes.he: לה כולה מתניתין כהדדי לכולה חמש חטאות המיתות בהדי אלא פליג ותני לה לתלת לחוד דימותו ולתרי לחוד. משום דרישא הני תלת קמאי פסיקא ליה. דבין לפני כפרה ובין לאחר כפרה מיתות:
notes.en: What is the reason it does not teach: the whole mishna together, all five sin offerings that die together, but divides it and teaches the three separately, that they shall die, and the two separately? Because in the first clause, these first three, it is absolute: whether before atonement or after atonement, they die.

messages.text: With regard to those sin offerings taught in the first clause, there is an absolute rule that applies equally in all circumstances. But with regard to the remaining types taught in the latter clause, there is no absolute rule, as these sin offerings are left to die only if the owner has already achieved atonement with another animal.

notes.he: דלעולם מתות ואפילו לא כיפרו הבעלים:
notes.en: The first clause is absolute: they always die, even if the owner has not achieved atonement.

messages.text: This mishna also appears in tractate Me’ila (10b). Why do I need the tanna to teach this mishna in tractate Me’ila and why do I need him to teach it in tractate Temura?

notes.he: דכולה הך מתני' תנינן גבי מעילה שיש שם פרק אחד שמתחיל ולד חטאת ותמורת חטאת וכולה מתניתין :
notes.en: Why do I need to teach it in connection with misuse: for this entire mishna is also taught in connection with misuse, as there is a chapter there [in Me’ila] that begins “The offspring of a sin offering and the substitute of a sin offering,” with the whole mishna.

messages.text: Here, in Temura, the mishna taught the halakhot pertaining to substitution, which is the central theme of tractate Temura. And since it taught the halakhot pertaining to substitution, it also taught the relevant halakhot pertaining to misuse of consecrated property. And similarly, since it taught in tractate Me’ila the halakhot pertaining to misuse of consecrated property, which is the subject of tractate Me’ila, it also taught the relevant halakhot pertaining to substitution.

notes.he: דהא לפני כפרה ירעו. ומאי טעמא תני לה בתמורה דקאמר ועושין תמורה והדר תני מועלין בה משום אגב דקאי בתמורה ואיידי דתנא תמורה תני ומועלין בה והתם במס' מעילה איכא פירקא דמתחיל נמי ולד חטאת כו'. ואיידי דהתם תני מעילה תנא נמי התם דתמורה:
notes.en: The latter clause is not absolute: for before atonement they graze. And what is the reason it teaches it in Temurah? For it says “and it renders a substitute,” and then it teaches “one is liable for misuse of it” incidentally, since it is dealing with substitution; and since it taught substitution, it taught “one is liable for misuse of it.” And there, in tractate Me’ila, there is a chapter that also begins “The offspring of a sin offering, etc.,” and since there it teaches misuse, there it also taught substitution.

messages.text: With regard to a sin offering whose first year from birth has passed, one considers it as though it is standing in a cemetery, where a priest cannot enter in order to retrieve it and sacrifice it, and it is left to graze until it develops a blemish, after which it is sold and the money received in its sale is used to purchase another animal for a sin offering.

notes.he: כלומר כל מקום שהיא שם רואין אותה כאילו היא עומדת בבית הקברות שאין כהן יכול ליכנס אחריה ולשוחטה ורועה עד שתסתאב:
notes.en: As though it is standing in a cemetery: that is, wherever it is, one views it as though it stands in a cemetery, where a priest cannot go in after it to slaughter it; and it grazes until it becomes blemished.

notes.he: אע"ג דקיימא בעזרה:
notes.en: A sin offering whose year has passed: even though it is standing in the Temple courtyard.

notes.dh: רואין אותה כאילו עומד בבית הקברות
notes.he: מה התם לא מצי כהן אזיל לאייתויי אף הכא נמי לא חזיא להקרבה אלא תרעה:
notes.en: One views it as though it stands in a cemetery: just as there a priest cannot go to bring it, so too here it is not fit for sacrifice; rather, it grazes.

messages.text: Since Reish Lakish makes no distinction between an owner who already achieved atonement with another animal and one who did not, it seems that according to Reish Lakish, this is the halakha in all cases of a sin offering whose first year from birth has passed.

We learned in the mishna: With regard to a sin offering whose first year from birth has passed and a sin offering that was lost and when it was found it was blemished, if it was after the owner achieved atonement through the sacrifice of another animal as a sin offering, the blemished animal is left to die. This is apparently a conclusive refutation of the opinion of Reish Lakish.

notes.dh: תנן חטאת שעיברה שנתה או שאבדה ונמצאת בעלת מום כו' תיובתא דר"ש בן לקיש
notes.he: דפסיק ואמר רועה ומשמע אפילו כיפרו הבעלים:
notes.en: We learned: a sin offering whose year has passed, or that was lost and found blemished, etc. A refutation of Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish: for he stated without distinction that it grazes, which implies even if the owner has achieved atonement.

notes.he: משמע דקאמר נמי אשעיברה שנתה]:
notes.en: [If after the owner achieved atonement, it shall die: this implies that it also refers to the one whose year has passed.]

messages.text: Reish Lakish could say to you: When the mishna teaches in the first clause that the animal is sequestered and left to die, it is referring only to the case where it was lost and when it was found it was blemished. In that situation, if it was after the owner achieved atonement through the sacrifice of another animal as a sin offering, the blemished animal shall be left to die. By contrast, a sin offering whose first year from birth has passed is indeed left to graze until it develops a blemish.

notes.dh: כי קתני מתה אאבדה ונמצאת בעלת מום
notes.he: ולקמן פריך א"כ עברה שנתה למאי הלכתא קתני לה בהדי הנך דמתות:
notes.en: When it teaches “dies,” it is about the one lost and found blemished: and below it asks: if so, with regard to what halakha does it teach the one whose year has passed together with those that die?

messages.text: If so, say the latter clause: If the lost animal was found and discovered to be unfit before the owner achieved atonement for his sin with a different animal, it shall graze until it becomes blemished. Now, if the mishna is referring specifically to an animal that was lost and found when it was blemished, why is this statement necessary? Doesn’t it already stand blemished?
messages.quote: before the owner achieved atonement … it shall graze until it becomes blemished

notes.he: [אמר לך ריש לקיש כי קתני תמורה אאבדה ונמצא בעל מום ולא אעיברה שנתה. ואי בעל מום למה לי תרעה אלא אעיברה שנתה קאמר תרעה] מדהא קא מיירי בעיברה שנתה אף משכיפרו בעלים תמות נמי מיירי בעיברה שנתה וקשיא לריש לקיש:
notes.en: If so, say the latter clause, etc.: [Reish Lakish could say to you: when it teaches “die,” it refers to one lost and found blemished, and not to one whose year has passed. But if it is blemished, why do I need “it shall graze”? Rather, it says “it shall graze” of the one whose year has passed.] Since this refers to one whose year has passed, “if after the owner achieved atonement it shall die” also refers to one whose year has passed, and this is difficult for Reish Lakish.

messages.text: This is what the tanna is saying: In a case where it was lost and subsequently found when it had a temporary blemish, then if it was after the owner achieved atonement with another sin offering, the blemished animal shall be left to die. But if this was before the owner achieved atonement with another sin offering, it shall graze until it becomes blemished with a permanent blemish, and then it shall be sold.

notes.he: שעברה שנתה או אבדה ונמצאת בעלת מום עובר לאחר שכיפרו הבעלים מתה ואפי' כיפרו הבעלים אחרי כן הואיל ואיכא תרתי לריעותא מתה ואעברה שנתה לא קאי כלל:
notes.en: Rabba said, this is what it is saying: [the words] “whose year has passed, or that was lost and found blemished” [mean] with a temporary blemish; after the owner achieved atonement, it dies. And even if the owner achieved atonement only afterward [i.e., after it was found], since there are two flaws, it dies. And [this ruling] does not refer to the one whose year has passed at all.

notes.he: כלומר שלא רצו להתכפר באחרת תרעה כו'. והשתא ליכא למיפרך הא מסאבא וקיימא דאין בהמת קדשים נמכרת על מום עובר:
notes.en: And if before the owner achieved atonement: that is, they did not want to achieve atonement with another, it shall graze, etc. And now one cannot object “but it already stands blemished,” since a consecrated animal is not sold on account of a temporary blemish.

notes.he: אמר רבה תני הכי אם עיברה שנתה [או] אבדה ונמצא בעל מום עובר (או אבדה) [ושאבדה] ונמצאת בעלת מום קבוע אם משכיפרו בעלים תמות דהכא איכא תרתי לריעותא דאבדה ונמצ' בעל מום הלכך תמות ולא קשיא סיפא נמי דכולה בחדא [מיירי] (איידי ואיהיא ואיהיא) תרעה עד שתסתאב במום קבוע:
notes.en: Rabba said: teach it thus: [a sin offering] whose year has passed, [or] that was lost and found with a temporary blemish, [or that was lost] and found with a permanent blemish: if after the owner achieved atonement, it shall die, for here there are two flaws, that it was lost and was found blemished; therefore it shall die. And the latter clause is not difficult either, for all of it deals with one [case] (the printed text is garbled here): it shall graze until it becomes blemished with a permanent blemish.

messages.text: There are two refutations of Rabba’s statement: One refutation is that if it is so, that the mishna is referring to an animal that was lost and then found when it had a temporary blemish, then instead of stating: It shall graze until it becomes blemished, the mishna should have taught: One observes the animal to see whether the temporary blemish becomes permanent. And furthermore, according to this interpretation of the mishna, when it mentions the case of a sin offering whose first year from birth has passed, with regard to what halakha is that case taught?
messages.quote: found when it had a temporary blemish

notes.he: כלומר הואיל וכבר נפל בה מום עובר ישמור מיבעי ליה למיתני כלומר ימתין אולי יעשה מום זה קבוע:
notes.en: It should have said “he shall watch”: that is, since a temporary blemish has already befallen it, it should have taught “he shall watch,” that is, he shall wait; perhaps this blemish will become permanent.

notes.dh: ועוד עברה שנתה למאי קתני לה
notes.he: הואיל ולאו עלה איירי שום דינא:
notes.en: And furthermore, with regard to what is “whose year has passed” taught: since no ruling at all is stated about it.

notes.he: פרש"י ישמור אותה אולי יעשה מום קבוע ול"נ דא"כ היינו תרעה דקתני לכן נראה לפרש ישמור אותה אולי תתרפא וחזיא להקרבה:
notes.en: It should have said “he shall watch”: Rashi explains: he shall watch it, perhaps it will become a permanent blemish. But this does not seem right to me, for if so, that is the same as “it shall graze,” which the mishna teaches. Therefore it seems one should explain: he shall watch it, perhaps it will heal and become fit for sacrifice.

notes.he: דבבעלת מום עובר קא מיירי אמאי קתני תרעה ישמור עד שיעשה מום קבוע (אידי) בעי למיתנא ועוד כיון דההיא שעיברה שנתה אם משכיפרו הבעלים לא תמות אא"כ אבדה ונמצאת בעלת מום לחוד למאי הלכתא קתני לה (א"כ לעיברה) [ההיא דעיברה] שנתה. ל"א ותוב כי קתני תמות אאבדה ונמצאת בעלת מום ולא אאעיברה שנתה [א"כ] למה תנייה לעיברה שנתה בין הני דמתניתין אלא אמר רבא (הכי קתני) [הכי נמי] שעיברה שנתה ואבדה וכן נמי ההיא דאבדה ונמצ' בעל מום אם משכיפרו הבעלים תמות משום דאית בכל חדא תרתי לריעותא ולא קשיא לריש לקיש והאי דקתני אם עד שלא כיפרו תרעה אעיברה שנתה לחוד קאי ולא אאבדה ונמצא בעל מום:
notes.en: For if so: that it deals with one with a temporary blemish, why does it teach “it shall graze”? It should have taught “he shall watch it until it gets a permanent blemish.” And furthermore, since one whose year has passed does not die if after the owner achieved atonement, unless it was lost and found blemished alone, for what halakha does it teach the one whose year has passed? Another version: And furthermore, when it teaches “die” of one lost and found blemished and not of one whose year has passed, [if so,] why does it teach the one whose year has passed among these of the mishna? Rather, Rava said: so too [it teaches]: one whose year has passed and was lost, and likewise the one that was lost and found blemished: if after the owner achieved atonement, it shall die, because each one has two flaws; and it is not difficult for Reish Lakish. And what it teaches, “if before the owner achieved atonement, it shall graze,” refers to the one whose year has passed alone, and not to the one lost and found blemished.

messages.text: This is what the mishna is teaching: With regard to a sin offering whose first year from birth has passed and was lost, or one that was lost and when it was found it was blemished, which means that in each case, there are two disqualifying factors, the halakha is as follows: If the first animal is found after the owner achieved atonement with another sin offering, the animal shall be left to die. If it is found before the owner achieved atonement with another sin offering, it shall graze until it becomes blemished and then it shall be sold.
messages.lead: Rather, a different explanation of the mishna, so that it does not contradict the statement of Reish Lakish:

notes.he: ונמצאת תמימה וכיפרו הבעלים באחרת או אבדה ונמצאת בעלת מום דאיכא נמי תרתי לריעותא וכיפרו הבעלים באחרת מתה קודם שכיפרו הבעלים שאין רוצים להתכפר באחרת תרעה הך דעברה שנתה ואבדה ונמצאת תמימה וכי אר"ש בן לקיש דאפי' כיפרו הבעלים אחרי כן רועה בלא אבדה דחדא הוא דאיכא לריעותא:
notes.en: Its year passed and it was lost: and it was found unblemished and the owner achieved atonement with another; or it was lost and found blemished, where there are also two flaws, and the owner achieved atonement with another: it dies. Before the owner achieved atonement, [i.e.] they do not want to achieve atonement with another: this one, whose year passed and which was lost and found unblemished, shall graze. And when Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said that even if the owner achieved atonement afterward it grazes, [that is] without a loss, for there is only one flaw.

messages.text: Reish Lakish, by contrast, is referring to a situation where the sin offering was not lost. In such a case there is only one disqualifying factor, and therefore the animal is left to graze regardless of whether or not the owner achieved atonement with another animal.

messages.caption: Rava’s reading: a sin offering dies after the owner’s atonement only when it was lost on top of another flaw.

messages.text: And it was necessary for the mishna to teach: If it was lost, with regard to a sin offering that was found to be blemished, and also to teach that clause with regard to a sin offering whose first year has passed. In other words, it was necessary for the mishna to teach that in each of these cases losing the animal means that it must be sequestered and left to die if the owner already achieved atonement with another animal.

As if it had taught this halakha only with regard to a sin offering whose first year has passed, I would say: It is only there that the fact that it was lost is effective in requiring that the animal must be left to die, because it is not fit for its original purpose, as an animal more than one year old is inherently unfit for a sin offering. But with regard to a blemished animal, which would have been fit for sacrifice if not for its blemish, I might say that the fact that it was lost is not effective in causing the animal to be left to die.

notes.he: מועלת בה להביאה למיתה:
notes.en: That the loss is effective for it: it works upon it to bring it to death.

notes.he: אפי' קודם אבידה דבת שנתה כתיב (במדבר טו) וזו עברה שנתה ופסול הגוף הוא:
notes.en: Because it is not fit for its purpose: even before the loss, for “in its first year” is written (Numbers 15:27), and this one’s year has passed; that is a disqualification of the body itself.

notes.he: פסול חסרון בעלמא והואיל ונמצאת קודם כפרת השניה תרעה ולא תיהני ליה אבידה למות:
notes.en: Which, if not for the blemish, would be fit, I would say: it is merely a disqualification of deficiency, and since it was found before the atonement of the second, it shall graze, and the loss should not be effective to make it die.

messages.text: And similarly, if the mishna had taught the halakha only with regard to a blemished animal, I would say: It is only there that the fact that it was lost is effective in requiring that the animal must be left to die, because a blemished animal is not fit for sacrifice at all. But with regard to a sin offering whose first year has passed, which is fit for sacrifice as a different offering, I might say that the fact that it was lost is not effective in causing the animal to be left to die. Consequently, it was necessary for the mishna to teach the halakha with regard to both cases.

notes.he: בשום קרבן:
notes.en: Because it is not fit for sacrifice: as any offering.

notes.he: בשאר קרבנות וכל הנך דבעיין תרתי לריעותא היינו כי נמצאת קודם כפרת שניה אבל נמצאת לאחר כפרה אפילו אין שם ריעותא דאיבוד מתה:
notes.en: One whose year has passed is fit for sacrifice: as other offerings. And all these cases that require two flaws are where it was found before the atonement of the second; but if it was found after the atonement, even if there is no flaw there [other than] the loss, it dies.

notes.dh: אי תניא גבי עיברה שנתה התם הוא דלא אהני (לה אבודה) משום דחזיא להקרבה
notes.he: והיינו כשיטת ר"י דריבוי ריעותות מביאין אותה לידי רעיה:
notes.en: If it had taught it with regard to one whose year has passed, there the loss is not effective, because it is fit for sacrifice [so Tosafot’s heading; the Gemara itself makes this point in its second clause]: and this follows the approach of the Ri, that many flaws bring it to grazing.

messages.text: And did Rava actually say this, that an animal whose first year has passed and was then lost is left to die? But didn’t Rava say: A sin offering lost at night is not called lost?
messages.quote: whose first year from birth has passed and was lost

notes.he: דהיכא דנפסלה קודם לאיבוד מהני לה איבוד למות:
notes.en: And did Rava say so: that where it was disqualified before the loss, the loss is effective to make it die?

notes.dh: והאמר רבא אבודת לילה לאו שמה אבודה
notes.he: אם אבדה בלילה והפריש אחרת תחתיה לאו שמה אבודה ולר' דאמר אפי' נמצאת קודם כפרה מתה האי אינה מתה דהואיל ובלילה לא מצי לאקרובה והיא נמצאת ביום המחרת לאו שמה אבודה ורועה אם נתכפר בחברתה. וה"נ הואיל ועברה שנתה לא חזיא לאקרובי לא תיהני ביה אבודה:
notes.en: But didn’t Rava say: one lost at night is not called lost: if it was lost at night and he set aside another in its place, it is not called lost. And according to Rabbi, who says that even if it is found before atonement it dies, this one does not die: since at night he could not sacrifice it, and it is found the next day, it is not called lost, and it grazes if he achieved atonement with its fellow. And here too, since one whose year has passed is not fit to be sacrificed, the loss should not be effective for it.

notes.he: דהיכא דנפסלה קודם האיבוד דמהניא ליה איבוד למות והאמר רבא אבודת לילה לא שמה אבודה וא"ת ליפרוך ממתני' דקתני אבדה ונמצאת בעלת מום מתה אע"ג דאיכא ריעותא אחריתי עם האבודה וי"ל דבשלמא ממתני' לא מצי למיפרך דשאני מתני' דאבדה קודם שיבא לה הריעותא אחריתי ומש"ה לא דמי לאבודת לילה דריעותא דלילה בא עליה קודם האיבוד אבל לרבא פריך שפיר שהרי ריעותא דעברה שנתה בא עליה קודם האיבוד ומש"ה פריך מאבודת לילה ומשני לא דמי אבודת לילה לא חזיא לא לגופה ולא לדמי כאן משמע כשיטת ר"י דריבוי ריעותות מביאין אותה לרעיה ולא למיתה:
notes.en: And did Rava say so: that where it was disqualified before the loss, the loss is effective to make it die? But didn’t Rava say: one lost at night is not called lost. And if you say: let it raise an objection from the mishna, which teaches that one lost and found blemished dies, even though there is another flaw together with the loss — one can say: granted, from the mishna it cannot object, for the mishna is different, since it was lost before the other flaw came upon it, and therefore it is not comparable to one lost at night, where the flaw of night came upon it before the loss. But against Rava it objects well, for the flaw of its year having passed came upon it before the loss, and that is why it objects from one lost at night. And it answers: one lost at night is not comparable; it is fit neither for itself nor for its value. Here it is implied, as in the approach of the Ri, that many flaws bring it to grazing and not to death.

messages.text: In other words, if the offering is lost at a time that it is not fit for sacrifice, the animal is not considered lost. Consequently, provided that the owner finds the sin offering before morning, it is left to graze and not to die, even if the owner designated another animal in its stead. By the same logic, as a sin offering whose first year has passed is not fit for sacrifice as a sin offering, it should not be considered lost even if the owner cannot locate it. Therefore, it should not be left to die.

notes.he: דשעיברה שנתה ואבדה דמשום הכי תמות משום דאבדה והאמר רבא אבודה דלילה ונמצא בשחרית לא שמה אבוד דלא מיפסלה באבידה דלילה משום דלילה לאו זמן הקרבה וכן נמי כי אבדה לאחר שעיברה שנתה דלא חזיא להקרבה לא תיפסל בה אבידה:
notes.en: And did Rava say so: that one whose year has passed and was lost dies on this account, because it was lost? But didn’t Rava say: one lost at night and found in the morning is not called lost, for it is not disqualified by a loss at night, since night is not a time of sacrifice. And likewise, when it was lost after its year had passed, when it was not fit for sacrifice, a loss should not disqualify it.

messages.text: The case of a sin offering lost at night is not comparable to that of a sin offering lost after its first year has passed. When a sin offering is lost at night, it is not fit at all, neither for itself, i.e., to be sacrificed, nor for its value, to be sold and the proceeds used to purchase another offering. But with regard to this sin offering that was lost after its first year has passed, granted that it is not fit for itself, but it is fit for its value.

notes.he: שאין דמיה ראויין ליקרב בשעת אבידתה דאין קרבן בלילה:
notes.en: Nor for its value: for its value is not fit to be sacrificed at the time of its loss, as there is no offering at night.

notes.he: קודם שאבדה:
notes.en: It is fit for its value: before it was lost.

notes.he: לא דמיא דאבודה דלילה להכי לא שמה אבודה דאותה אבודה דלילה לא חזיא לא לקדושת הגוף ליקרב עצמה בלילה ולא לקדושת דמים למוכרה ולהביא אחרת תחתיה בלילה אבל שעיברה שנתה ואבדה ונמצא נהי דלקדושת הגוף ליקרב עצמה דהא עיברה שנתה לא חזיא לקדושת דמים למוכרה ולהביא בדמיה אחרת חזיא וכיון דבשעת אבידה חזיא לקדושת דמים הלכך פסלה לה אבדה ותמות:
notes.en: Rava holds: one lost at night is not comparable; that is why it is not called lost. For that one lost at night is fit neither for sanctity of the body, to be sacrificed itself at night, nor for sanctity of value, to sell it and bring another in its place at night. But one whose year has passed and was lost and found: granted that for sanctity of the body, to be sacrificed itself, it is not fit, since its year has passed; for sanctity of value, to sell it and bring another with its money, it is fit. And since at the time of the loss it was fit for sanctity of value, the loss therefore disqualifies it, and it shall die.

messages.text: Another challenge to the opinion of Rava: We learned in a mishna (Yoma 62a):

On Yom Kippur, a pair of goats are brought to the Temple, and lots are drawn to determine which goat is to be sent to Azazel as the scapegoat, and which goat is sacrificed as a sin offering. If after the lots were drawn for both goats, the scapegoat died, another pair of goats is brought and lots are drawn for the second pair. In such a case, there are two goats that were selected as the sin offering, i.e., the remaining goat from the first pair and the goat selected from the second. One of them is sacrificed and the second goat shall graze until it becomes blemished, at which point it will be sold, and the money received from its sale will be allocated for communal gift offerings. This is because a communal sin offering is not left to die.

notes.he: במסכת יומא (דף סב.) גבי שעירי יום הכפורים מת אותו של עזאזל מביא שנים מן השוק ומגריל ומשלח האחד והשני ירעה עד שיסתאב:
notes.en: We learned: in tractate Yoma (62a), concerning the goats of Yom Kippur: if the one for Azazel died, he brings two from the market and draws lots, and sends one away, and the second shall graze until it becomes blemished.

notes.he: [תנן במסכת יומא מת אחד מן השעירים עד שלא הגרילו עליהן יביא אחר ומזויג לו ואם משהגריל יביא שנים אחרים ויגריל עליהן ויאמר אם של שם מת זה שעלה עליו הגורל לשם יתקיים תחתיו ואם של עזאזל מת כו'. עד והשני ירעה עד שיסתאב ויפלו דמיו לנדבה לפי שאין חטאת הציבור מתה. כדאמר לעיל בפ' יש בקרבנות]:
notes.en: [We learned in tractate Yoma: if one of the goats died before the lots were drawn over them, he brings another and pairs it with it; and if after the lots were drawn, he brings two others and draws lots over them and says: if the one for the Name died, this one on which the lot for the Name came up shall stand in its place; and if the one for Azazel died, etc., up to: and the second shall graze until it becomes blemished, and its money goes to gift offerings, since a communal sin offering does not die. As was said above in the chapter Yesh BaKorbanot.]

messages.text: One may infer from the mishna that under similar circumstances, the sin offering of an individual is left to die.
messages.quote: because a communal sin offering is not left to die

notes.he: כי האי גוונא מתה:
notes.en: But an individual’s: in a case like this, it dies.

messages.text: The goat from the second pair is sacrificed, since living animals are rejected. That is, animals that were consecrated for a specific purpose but were not fit to be used for that purpose at the proper time are permanently disqualified as a sacrifice. Accordingly, as the first goat was unfit for sacrifice when the first scapegoat died, it is permanently disqualified from the altar. And therefore, when the High Priest achieves atonement on behalf of the Jewish people, he achieves atonement with the second goat of the second pair [zug].
messages.lead: And as the mishna does not specify which of the two goats is sacrificed as the sin offering:

notes.he: במסכת יומא (דף סד.) בעלי חיין נדחין ונדחה שני שבזוג ראשון כשמת חבירו לעולם וכשהוא מתכפר מתכפר בשני שבזוג שני וקמא הוי דחוי כשמת חבירו כאילו עברה שנתו. וקתני דטעמא דאינה מתה משום דחטאת צבור היא הא דיחיד מת ואע"ג דליכא שום אבידה מת משום דיחוי דקמא מאחר שנתכפר באחר אלמא תרתי לריעותא לא בעינן וקשיא לרבא:
notes.en: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said: in tractate Yoma (64a): living animals are rejected. The second of the first pair is rejected forever when its fellow died, and when he achieves atonement, he achieves atonement with the second of the second pair. And the first was rejected when its fellow died, as though its year had passed. And it teaches that the reason it does not die is that it is a communal sin offering; but an individual’s dies, and even though there is no loss at all, it dies because of the rejection of the first, since he achieved atonement with another. Evidently we do not require two flaws, and this is difficult for Rava.

messages.text: And the other goat, i.e., the first goat selected as the sin offering, is like a sin offering whose first year has passed, in that both are disqualified due to an external factor. And the Gemara infers that the reason the first goat is not left to die is that it is a communal sin offering; but if it was the sin offering of an individual, it would be left to die. Evidently, a sin offering whose first year has passed is left to die even if it was not lost.

notes.he: התם בעלי חיים שהיו ראויין ולא אירע בעצמו פסול נידחין מהקרבה וכשהוא מתכפר בשני שבזוג שני מתכפר שלא מת אחד מהן ואידך קמא שמת חברו כיון דעבר זמנו דנתכפרו באחר הוה ליה כי עיברה שנתה וטעמא דציבור דרועה הא דיחיד מתה וקשיא לרבא דאמר שעיברה שנתה ואבדה אם נמצא עד שלא כיפרו הבעלים תרעה והא הכא דאיתיה להאי [קמא] דקאי עד שלא כיפרו הבעלים וטעמא דציבור הוא הא דיחיד מתה אמר לך רבא דחויין לחוד הא משום הכי הוה מיית אי הוה דיחיד דדחוי הוא לגמרי מהקרבה ואבודין לחוד דלא מסח דעתיה מינייהו דסבר מישתכחי (הילכת') [הלכך] ירעו:
notes.en: And Rabbi Yoḥanan said: there, living animals that were fit, and no disqualification befell them themselves, are rejected from sacrifice; and when he achieves atonement, he achieves atonement with the second of the second pair, neither of which died. And the other, the first, whose fellow died: since its time has passed, as he achieved atonement with another, it is like one whose year has passed. And the reason is that it is communal, so it grazes; but an individual’s dies. And this is difficult for Rava, who said that one whose year has passed and was lost, if it was found before the owner achieved atonement, grazes; but here this [first] one is present, standing before the owner achieved atonement, and the reason is that it is communal; but an individual’s dies. Rava could say to you: the rejected are discrete — that is why it would die if it were an individual’s, for it is entirely rejected from sacrifice; and the lost are discrete, for he does not put them out of his mind, as he thinks they will be found; therefore they graze.

messages.text: Rava could say to you: The case of sin offerings that were rejected is discrete and the case of sin offerings that were lost is discrete, i.e., the two cases cannot be compared. What is the reason for this? In the case of lost sin offerings, the owner’s mind is on them, as he thinks that perhaps they will be found and will be fit for sacrifice. Therefore, they are not left to die simply because they are lost. But in the case of sin offerings that have been rejected, they do not become fit ever again, and therefore the owner’s mind is not on them.

notes.he: רבא ודאי איכא דיחוי ונתכפר באחר מתה בלא שום אבידה ולר"ל ודאי תיקשי וכדתריצנא לעיל עברה שנתה ואבדה לר"ל תריצנא ולדידי לא סבירא לי ואי משום אבדה ונמצאת בעלת מום קשיא לך אמאי נקט בעלת מום תמות משום אבדה לחודה הואיל ושוב נתכפר באחרת לא קשיא דחויין לחוד ואבודין לחוד ואע"ג דאבדה בעינן ריעותא אחריתי. כך שמעתי לא יותר:
notes.en: [Rava] could say to you: certainly, where there is rejection and he achieved atonement with another, it dies without any loss, and for Reish Lakish this is certainly difficult. And as for what I answered above, “its year passed and it was lost,” I answered that for Reish Lakish, but I myself do not hold so. And if the case of “lost and found blemished” is difficult for you — why did it specify blemished; let it die because of the loss alone, since he then achieved atonement with another — that is not difficult: the rejected are discrete and the lost are discrete, and although it was lost we require another flaw. So I heard, and no more.

notes.he: פרש"י ודאי היכא דאיכא דיחוי ונתכפר באחרת מתה בלא שום אבודה ולרשב"ל ודאי תקשה דכי תריצנא לעיל עברה שנתה ואבדה לרשב"ל תריצנא ולי לא סבירא לי ואי משום אבדה ונמצאת בעלת מום קשיא לך אמאי נקט בעלת מום תמות משום אבודה לחודה הואיל ושוב נתכפר באחרת לא קשיא דחויין לחוד ואבודין לחוד ואע"ג דאבדה בעינן ריעותא אחריתי עכ"ל ולא נראה דתשאר מילתא דרשב"ל בקושיא דהא מייתי לה בכמה מקומות בהש"ס ועוד קשה דממה שהקשה לא תירץ לכך נראה לר"י לפרש כי היכי דאיצטריך לשנויי אמתני' דבעי תרתי אבודה ובעלת מום ולפיכך אתה צריך לחלק ולומר דחויין לחוד ואבודין לחוד הכי נמי נתרץ לרשב"ל דחויין לחוד ועברה שנתה לחוד דחויין לא חזו לשום הקרבה ועברה שנתה חזיה להקרבה דשאר קרבנות:
notes.en: Rava could say to you: Rashi explains: certainly, where there is rejection and he achieved atonement with another, it dies without any loss; and for Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish it is certainly difficult, for when I answered above “its year passed and it was lost,” I answered it for Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish, but I do not hold so; and if “lost and found blemished” is difficult for you, why did it specify blemished, let it die on account of the loss alone since he then achieved atonement with another — that is not difficult: the rejected are discrete and the lost are discrete, and although it was lost we require another flaw. End of his words. But this does not seem right, that the statement of Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish should be left refuted, for it is cited in several places in the Talmud. And furthermore, it is difficult that he has not answered what was asked. Therefore it seems to the Ri to explain: just as it was necessary to answer for the mishna, which requires two [flaws], loss and a blemish, so that you must distinguish and say the rejected are discrete and the lost are discrete, so too we answer for Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish: the rejected are discrete and one whose year has passed is discrete. The rejected are not fit for any sacrifice, while one whose year has passed is fit for sacrifice as other offerings.

notes.dh: ל"א אלמא הואיל דאי דחיית לה כו'
notes.he: כלישנא קמא לית בינייהו אלא שינוי לשון:
notes.en: Another version: “Evidently, since if you reject it, etc.” [It is] like the first version; there is nothing between them but a difference of wording.

messages.text: The matter itself, which was cited above:

A sin offering lost at night, when one cannot sacrifice an offering, is not called lost. Provided that the offering is found before morning, then even if the owner designated another sin offering in its stead, the first sin offering is not left to die.

notes.he: קס"ד דלא היתה אבודה אלא בלילה ובעלות השחר נמצאת ולא משכחת לה דתיהוי אבודה בשעת כפרה דהא בלילה לא קרבה חברתה:
notes.en: The matter itself: one lost at night. We assume at first that it was lost only during the night and was found at dawn, so you cannot find it lost at the time of atonement, for at night its fellow is not sacrificed.

messages.text: In accordance with whose opinion is this statement? If we say that it is in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis, who maintain that a sin offering is not left to die unless the owner achieved atonement with another offering, why does Rava specifically mention that it was lost at night? Even if it was lost during the day it is not left to die, as the Rabbis say: A sin offering that was lost at the time when another animal was designated in its stead, but was found before this second animal was sacrificed, is left to graze until it develops a blemish.
messages.quote: lost at night, is not called lost

notes.he: שנמצאת קודם כפרת חברתה:
notes.en: Even one lost by day too: that was found before the atonement of its fellow.

notes.he: במתני' אבודה בשעת הפרשה כלומר בשעה שעדיין חברתה שהפריש תחתיה מופרשת ועומדת שלא קרבה קודם מציאתה של זו רועה דקתני וחכמים אומרים אין חטאת מתה אלא שנמצאת לאחר שנתכפרו הבעלים:
notes.en: For the Rabbis say: in the mishna, [one] lost at the time of designation, that is, while its fellow that he set aside in its place was still set aside and standing, and was not sacrificed before this one was found, grazes; as it teaches: And the Rabbis say: A sin offering dies only if it was found after the owner achieved atonement.

notes.dh: אפי' אבודה דיממא נמי דאמרי רבנן אבודה בשעת הפרשה רועה
notes.he: ואם תאמר לימא דלרבי אבא איצטריך דאמר לקמן (תמורה כג.) הכל מודים בנתכפר בשאינה אבודה אבודה מתה ואיצטריך רבנן לאשמועינן דאבודת לילה ונתכפר בשאינה אבודה אבודה אינה מתה הא דיממא כה"ג מתה וצריך לומר דהאי שיטה לית ליה דרבי אבא ה"נ איכא סוגיות בפרק מי שהיה טמא (פסחים דף צז.) דלא מיתוקמי כרבי אבא:
notes.en: Even one lost by day too, as the Rabbis say: one lost at the time of designation grazes. And if you say: let it say that [Rava’s statement] is needed according to Rabbi Abba, who says below (Temurah 23a): all agree that if he achieved atonement with the one that was not lost, the lost one dies; and [Rava] needed to teach us, according to the Rabbis, that one lost at night, where he achieved atonement with the one not lost, the lost one does not die, whereas one lost by day in such a case dies — one must say that this discussion does not hold like Rabbi Abba. So too there are discussions in the chapter Mi SheHaya Tamei (Pesaḥim 97a) that cannot be established according to Rabbi Abba.

notes.he: אילימא אליבא דרבנן דפליגי עליה דרבי במתניתין המפריש חטאת ואבדה והפריש אחרת תחתיה ולא הספיק כו':
notes.en: If we say according to the Rabbis: who disagree with Rabbi in the mishna: one who designates a sin offering and it was lost, and he designated another in its place and did not manage, etc.

notes.he: דיממא (בהדא) דאבודה היא בשעת הפרשה דשניה ולא בשעת כפרה ואמור רבנן עליה דרועה דלא שמה אבודה למות אבודה דלילה לא כ"ש:
notes.en: Now, one lost at the time of designation: by day, which is lost at the time of the second one’s designation and not at the time of atonement, and the Rabbis said of it that it grazes, for it is not called lost so as to die; one lost at night, all the more so.

messages.text: Rather, you must say that it is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, who maintains that if a sin offering was lost at the time when another animal was designated in its stead, the first sin offering is left to die even if it was found before the second animal was sacrificed. Rava teaches that Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi states his opinion only with regard to an animal lost during the day, but if the animal was lost only at night, even Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi concedes that it goes to graze and is not left to die.

notes.he: דאמר תמות וקמ"ל רבא דעד כאן לא קאמר רבי כו' לרעיה אזלא הואיל ואי נמי קיימא לקמן לא מצי לאקרובה בלילה לאו אבודה היא:
notes.en: Rather, according to Rabbi: who says it shall die. And Rava teaches us that Rabbi says so only, etc.; [one lost at night] goes to grazing, since even if it were standing before us, he could not sacrifice it at night; it is not lost.

notes.he: דפליג עלייהו דרבנן קאמר ולא קשיא דע"כ לא קאמר ר' כו':
notes.en: Rather, according to Rabbi: who disagrees with the Rabbis, he said it; and it is not difficult, for Rabbi says so only, etc.

messages.text: If you wish, say: Actually, Rava’s statement is in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis. And as for the question of why Rava specifies that it is lost only at night when the same halakha should apply even if it was lost during the day, one may respond: Here we are dealing with an animal that is still lost at the time when the owner achieves atonement with another animal.

notes.he: שאבדה בלילה ושוב לא נמצאת עד שנתכפר באחרת:
notes.en: At the time of atonement: it was lost at night and was not found again until he had achieved atonement with another.

notes.he: קאמר:
notes.en: And if you wish, say: actually, he said it according to the Rabbis.

notes.he: כגון שנאבדה בלילה ועדיין היתה אבודה ביום בשעת כפרה ואחר [כך] נמצאת:
notes.en: And here, with what are we dealing: for example, where it was lost at night and was still lost by day, at the time of atonement, and afterward it was found.

messages.text: Rava teaches that when the Rabbis say that a sin offering that remained lost at the time when the owner achieved atonement with another animal is left to die, this applies only where the initial loss of the animal was during the day, when the animal could have been sacrificed. But in a case where the initial loss of the animal was at night, it is not left to die. According to this interpretation, Rava is not merely saying that a sin offering is not classified as lost provided that it is found before morning. Rather, he maintains if it was initially lost at night it is never considered lost at all.

notes.he: תחילת אבידתה:
notes.en: The initial loss: the beginning of its being lost.

notes.he: וע"כ לא קאמרי רבנן אבודה בשעת כפרה מתה אלא היכא דעיקר אבידתה ביום אבל הכא דעיקר תחילת אבידתה בלילה הוה לא מתה אלא רועה:
notes.en: And the Rabbis say that one lost at the time of atonement dies only where its initial loss was by day; but here, where the very beginning of its loss was at night, it does not die but grazes.

messages.text: We have a tradition that a sin offering that was lost is left to die, but not a sin offering that was stolen; a sin offering that was lost is left to die, but not a sin offering that was robbed. If a sin offering was stolen or robbed, and the animal was returned after the owner achieved atonement with another animal, the first sin offering is left to graze until it develops a blemish, after which it is sold, and the proceeds are used to purchase a gift offering.

notes.he: בשעת כפרה מתה:
notes.en: We have a tradition: lost: [if lost] at the time of atonement, it dies.

notes.he: ואם החזירה לו לאחר כפרה רועה ויפלו דמיה לנדבה:
notes.en: And not stolen: and if it was returned to him after the atonement, it grazes and its money goes to gift offerings.

notes.he: דקא מיירי מתניתין אבודה ממש ולא גנובה וגזולה. דאבודה גמירי:
notes.en: We have a tradition: that the mishna is speaking of an actual lost [animal], and not one stolen or robbed; for [the rule of] a lost one we know by tradition.

messages.text: What are the circumstances in which an animal is considered to be lost?

Even one sin offering intermingled with other animals in the owner’s flock, to the extent that he cannot discern which animal is the sin offering, is considered lost. And even one sin offering intermingled with one non-sacred animal, so that the owner does not know which is the sin offering, is considered lost.

notes.he: שנתערבה לו בעדרו אע"ג דקא חזי לכולהו הואיל ואינו מכיר בה אלא לאחר כפרה הויא אבודה:
notes.en: One in his flock: that became intermingled in his flock; even though he sees all of them, since he does not recognize it until after the atonement, it is lost.

notes.he: של חטאת באחת של חולין:
notes.en: And even one: of a sin offering, with one non-sacred animal.

notes.he: בתוך עדרו ואינו מכירה או אפילו אחת חטאת באחת של חולין ואינו יודע אי זו היא של חטאת:
notes.en: For example, where one sin offering got mixed up within his flock and he does not recognize it, or even one sin offering with one non-sacred animal, and he does not know which is the sin offering.

messages.text: An animal found behind the door is considered to have been lost.

notes.he: ואין אדם רואה אותה:
notes.en: Or if it [ran off] behind the door, and no one sees it.

messages.text: With regard to what case is he speaking? Does Rabbi Yoḥanan mean that it is only when the animal is found behind the door that it is considered to have been lost, as there is no one who sees it, but if the animal was outside and was intermingled with other animals, where there are people who see it, it is not considered to be lost?
messages.lead: A dilemma was raised before the Sages with regard to the statement of Rabbi Yoḥanan:

notes.he: שהלכה למדברות ונתערבה בבהמות של אחרים ואותן אחרים עצמן אינם מכירין בה אפילו הכי כיון דאיכא דחזי לה דאותן אחרים חזו לה ואע"ג דאין מכירין אותה לא הויא אבודה:
notes.en: But outside: it went off into the wilderness and became intermingled with other people’s animals, and those others themselves do not recognize it. Even so, since there is someone who sees it, for those others see it, even though they do not recognize it, it is not lost.

notes.he: אם ברחה חוץ דאיכא שם אדם דקא חזי ליה:
notes.en: But outside: if it ran off outside, where there is someone who sees it.

messages.text: Or perhaps Rabbi Yoḥanan means that even when the animal is found behind the door, where if he would turn his face he would see it, the animal is considered lost, and all the more so if the animal was outside, where he does not see it, it is considered lost?

notes.dh: וכל שכן אבראי דלא קא חזי לה
notes.he: איהו לגמרי:
notes.en: And all the more so outside, where he does not see it: at all.

notes.dh: או דילמא אחורי הדלת דאי מהדר אפיה
notes.he: בעל הבהמה להתם הוה חזי ליה ואפי' הכי כל כמה דלא חזי ליה (הויא) [חשובה] אבידה וכל שכן אבראי דלא חזי ליה כלל:
notes.en: Or perhaps behind the door, where if the owner of the animal turned his face there he would see it, and even so, so long as he does not see it, it is [considered] lost; and all the more so outside, where he does not see it at all.

messages.text: Since no resolution is offered, the dilemma shall stand unresolved.

notes.he: ל"א אבל בעדר דקחזי לה דהא חזי להו איהו לכולהו אע"ג דאין מכיר בה לא הויא אבודה:
notes.en: Another version: but in the flock, where he sees it, for he sees all of them, even though he does not recognize it, it is not lost.

notes.he: כלומר שיפרישנו מהן לאחר זמן כשיכירנה:
notes.en: Ufeligei [a word in Rashi’s other version of the dilemma, which he takes to mean separating]: that is, he will separate it from them later, when he recognizes it.

notes.he: שאינו מכיר אי זו היא תיבעי תיקו [ע"כ ל"א]:
notes.en: That he does not know: that he does not recognize which one it is. Let it stand unresolved. [End of the other version.]

notes.he: דקא חזי ליה אבל אינו מכירה לא הוי אבודה דאמרינן דלמא מידכר סימניה ומוציאה מן העדר ופליג עליה [דר"א]:
notes.en: Another version: but [if] it got mixed up in the flock, where he sees it but does not recognize it, it is not lost, for we say: perhaps he will remember its marks and take it out of the flock. And [Rabbi Yoḥanan] disagrees with [Rabbi Oshaya].

messages.text: We learn through tradition that if a sin offering is lost from the owner but is not lost from the shepherd of the flock, i.e., the shepherd knows which animal is the sin offering, it is not considered lost. And all the more so, if the animal is lost from the shepherd but not lost from the owner, it is not considered lost.

notes.he: שאינו מכירה:
notes.en: Lost from him: that he does not recognize it.

notes.he: שהרועה מכירה:
notes.en: And not lost from the shepherd: that the shepherd recognizes it.

messages.text: If the sin offering was lost from the owner and the shepherd, but there is one individual located far away, even at the end of the world, who recognizes the animal, what is the halakha? The dilemma shall stand unresolved.

In a case where a sin offering was lost, and the owner designated another sin offering in its stead, and the second sin offering was slaughtered, what is the halakha if the original sin offering was found after the blood of the second offering was collected in a cup and stands ready to be sprinkled upon the altar?

notes.he: אבודה בשעה שדם חברתה בכוס שאבדה והפריש אחרת ושחטה וקיבל דמה ובעודו דם בכוס נמצאת זו:
notes.en: Lost in the cup: lost at the time its fellow’s blood is in the cup: it was lost, and he set aside another and slaughtered it and collected its blood, and while the blood was still in the cup, this one was found.

notes.he: שהיתה אבודה עד שעה שכבר קבלו דמה של חברתה בכוס ואח"כ נמצאת קודם זריקה אי אליבא דרבי יש לומר אבודה בשעת הפרשה חברתה בלבד א"ר מתה אבודה בכוס כ"ש]:
notes.en: [Lost in the cup: it stayed lost until they had already collected its fellow’s blood in the cup, and afterward it was found before the sprinkling. If according to Rabbi, one can say: if of one lost only at the time of its fellow’s designation Rabbi said it dies, one lost in the cup all the more so.]

messages.text: In accordance with whose opinion does Rav Pappa raise this dilemma? If we say that he raises it in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, this cannot be correct, as didn’t Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi say that even a sin offering that was lost at the time when another animal was merely designated in its stead is left to die?

notes.he: כלומר שנמצאת בעוד שחברתה קיימא מתה וכל שכן הכא שנשחטה כבר ואיכא למימר כל העומד ליזרק כזרוק דמי וכאבודה בשעת כפרה דמיא:
notes.en: Didn’t he say lost at the time of designation: that is, if it was found while its fellow was still standing [alive], it dies; all the more so here, where it was already slaughtered, and one could say: whatever stands to be sprinkled is considered sprinkled, and it is like one lost at the time of atonement.

messages.text: Rather, when Rav Pappa raises the dilemma, he does so according to the opinion of the Rabbis, and the dilemma is as follows: Do we say that when the Rabbis said: A sin offering that was lost at the time when another animal was designated in its stead is left to graze, this applies only if the original animal was found before one collects the blood of the other sin offering in a cup; but here, where the other sin offering was already slaughtered and its blood was collected in a cup, the Rabbis hold: Any blood that stands ready to be sprinkled upon the altar is considered like it has already been sprinkled, and it is as though the owner has achieved atonement? If so, this sin offering that was found after the collection of the blood should be left to die.

notes.dh: כי אמרו רבנן אבודה בשעת הפרשה רועה
notes.he: ואפי' נתכפרו הבעלים שוב באחרת הני מילי שנמצאת קודם שנתקבל דמה של חברתה בכוס אבל הכא כו':
notes.en: When the Rabbis said lost at the time of designation grazes: even if the owner then achieved atonement with another, that applies where it was found before its fellow’s blood was collected in the cup; but here, etc.

messages.text: Or perhaps the Rabbis maintain that as long as the blood has not been sprinkled on the altar, it is still considered like a case where the original offering was lost at the time when another animal was designated in its stead but was found by the time the second offering was brought to the altar. If so, as the first sin offering was found before the sprinkling of the blood, it should be left to graze until it develops a blemish.

And there are those who say an alternate explanation of the dilemma: Actually, Rav Pappa raises his dilemma according to the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi. And when Rav Pappa raises the dilemma, it is not with regard to a case involving two sin offerings, as described above. Rather, it is with regard to a case where the original sin offering was slaughtered and the priest collected its blood in two cups, and one of them was lost at the time when the priest sprinkled the blood of the remaining cup.

notes.he: ולאו בשתי בהמות מיבעי ליה אלא בבהמה אחת שקבל את דמה בשני כוסות:
notes.en: Actually, according to Rabbi: and he does not ask about two animals, but about one animal whose blood he collected in two cups.

notes.he: בשעת זריקת חבירו:
notes.en: And one of them was lost: at the time its fellow was sprinkled.

notes.he: ואי בעי תימא אפי' לר' קא מיבעיא ליה ולא מיבעיא ליה אבידה היא עצמה הבהמה אלא הכי קא מיבעיא ליה כגון שקבל דמה בב' כוסות ואבד אחד מהן ואליבא דמאן דאמר במס' יומא בפ' הוציאו לו [כוס עושה חברו דחוי דהכי קאמר התם למעלה הוא אומר בשעיר נשיא ואת כל דמו ישפוך ולמטה הוא אומר בשעירת יחיד ואת כל דמה ישפוך:
notes.en: And if you wish, say: he asks it even according to Rabbi, and he does not ask about the loss of the animal itself; rather, this is what he asks: for example, where he collected its blood in two cups and one of them was lost, and according to the one who said in tractate Yoma, in the chapter Hotziu Lo: [a cup renders its fellow rejected. For so it says there: above, regarding the goat of a prince, it says “And all its blood he shall pour out,” and below, regarding the female goat of an individual, it says “And all its blood he shall pour out.”

messages.text: And you should not raise the dilemma according to the opinion of the one who said that when blood is collected in two cups, one cup renders the blood of the other cup rejected, as in such a case, the entire offering is disqualified. Rather, when should you raise the dilemma? Raise it according to the opinion of the one who says that one cup renders the other cup a remainder, i.e., the blood in the second cup is considered the remainder of the first cup and is poured out at the base of the altar.

notes.he: במסכת יומא בפרק הוציאו לו בכוס אחד עושה את חבירו דיחוי דחטאת שקיבל דמה בארבע כוסות ונתן מן האחת ארבע מתנות כדין חטאת עשאן לאלו דחויין ושיריו נשפכין ליסוד והן נשפכין לאמה (דהא איתכשר בארבע מתנות אבל הכא דאבד האחד) לא תיבעי לך דודאי פסולה החטאת דהתם דכולהו לקמן הוא דהוי הזבח כשר אע"ג דהג' כוסות נשפכין לאמה דהא איתכשר בד' מתנות אבל הכא דאבד האחד כיון דאילו הוה קמן הוי דיחוי לישפך לאמה השתא כי אבד הוי להו תרתי לריעותא כחטאת שעברה שנתה ואבדה והזבח גופיה פסול:
notes.en: According to the one who said: in tractate Yoma, in the chapter Hotziu Lo: a cup renders its fellow rejected: [that is, regarding] a sin offering whose blood he collected in four cups and from one of them he placed the four placements, as the law of a sin offering requires, he has made those [others] rejected: its remainder is poured out at the base, and they are poured out into the channel. (For it was rendered fit with the four placements; but here, where one was lost.) You need not ask, for certainly the sin offering is disqualified. For there, where all of them are before us, the offering is fit, even though the three cups are poured into the channel, since it was rendered fit with four placements. But here, where one was lost: since had it been before us it would be rejected, to be poured into the channel, now that it is lost there are two flaws, like a sin offering whose year has passed and was lost, and the offering itself is disqualified.

notes.he: שכולן נשפכים ליסוד אבל הכא דאבדה מהניא ליה אבודה למיהוי דיחוי דלאו אדעתא דידיה זריק והוה ליה דיחוי ואבוד ופסול הזבח:
notes.en: Remainder: that all of them are poured out at the base. But here, where it was lost, the loss is effective to make it rejected, since he did not sprinkle with it in mind; so it is rejected and lost, and the offering is disqualified.

notes.dh: מניין לחטאת שקבל דמה בד' כוסות
notes.he: ונתן (ד' מתנות מכוס אחד) [מתנה אחת מזה ומתנה אחת מזה] שכולם האחרים נעשו שיריים ונשפכים ליסוד ת"ל ואת כל דמה ישפך אל יסוד יכול לא נתן אלא (מתנה אחת) [ד' מתנות] מאחת מהן שהאחרים נשפכין ליסוד ת"ל ואת (כל) דמו של אותו כוס בלבד ישפוך ליסוד והן האחרי' נשפכין לאמה (לזבל והינו) ואליבא דמאן דאמ' כוס עושה חברו דחוי שאינו נשפך ליסוד אלא לאמה לא תיבעי לך דהאי נמי כי אבד דמי דלא מצי [זריק] ליה כ"ש דהוי דחוי:
notes.en: From where [is it derived] that a sin offering whose blood he collected in four cups, and he placed [one placement from this and one placement from that], all of them, the others, become remainder and are poured out at the base? The verse states: “And all its blood he shall pour out at the base.” One might think that [even if] he placed [the four placements] from one of them, the others are poured out at the base; the verse states: “And its blood” — of that cup alone — he shall pour out at the base, and the others are poured out into the channel.] And according to the one who says a cup renders its fellow rejected, so that it is not poured out at the base but into the channel, you need not ask, for this one too, when it was lost, since he could not [sprinkle] it, all the more so it is rejected.

messages.text: The dilemma is as follows: Do we say that this statement, that the second cup is considered the remainder of the first cup, applies only in a case where both cups are present, since with whichever cup the priest wants, he may sprinkle; but here, since one of the cups is not present, the missing cup is therefore considered rejected and the offering is disqualified? Or perhaps it makes no difference whether both cups are present or not. The dilemma shall stand unresolved.

notes.he: או דלמא לא שנא תיבעי:
notes.en: Or perhaps there is no difference: let it stand unresolved.

notes.dh: כי תבעי לך אליבא דמאן דאמר כוס עושה חברו שירים
notes.he: היינו ר"א ב"ר שמעון [דאמר מניין שאפי' לא נתן אלא (מתנה אחת) [ד' מתנות] מכוס אחד שכולן נשפכין ליסוד ת"ל ואת כל דמה ישפך והא כת' ואת כל דמו ישפוך ההוא למעוטי שירים שבצואר בהמה דנשפכין לאמה מאי] מי אמרינן כי אמרינן כוס עושה חברו שירים הני מילי כי איתינון לתרויהון דלא נאבד אחד מהן אבל אבד אחד מהן מהניא ביה אבידה והוי דחוי או דלמא לא שנא דאפילו (אבד) [הכי] לא מיפסל אידך תיבעי. ול"א האי נמי קאמר אלא דמשני לשון:
notes.en: When should you ask it? According to the one who said a cup renders its fellow remainder; that is Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon, [who said: from where [is it derived] that even if he placed the four placements from one cup, all of them are poured out at the base? The verse states: “And all its blood he shall pour out.” And as for what is written, “And all its blood he shall pour out,” that serves to exclude the remainder in the animal’s neck, which is poured out into the channel. What is the halakha?] Do we say: when we say a cup renders its fellow remainder, that applies where both are present and neither of them was lost; but if one of them was lost, the loss is effective for it and it is rejected? Or perhaps there is no difference, and even so the other is not disqualified? Let it stand unresolved. And the other version says the same, only it changes the wording.

messages.text: Mishna

In the case of one who designates a sin offering, and the animal was lost, and he designated another in its stead and sacrificed it, and thereafter the first animal was found; that is a sin offering whose owner achieved atonement with another animal, and it shall be left to die.

notes.he: ואפי' נמצאת תמימה הואיל וכבר כיפרו הבעלים דכי בעינן תרתי לריעותא היכא דנמצאת ואחר כך כיפרו הבעלים:
notes.en: Mishna. And afterward the first was found, it shall die: even if it was found unblemished, since the owner has already achieved atonement. For where we require two flaws is where it was found and afterward the owner achieved atonement.

notes.dh: המפריש חטאת ואבדה והקריב אחרת תחתיה ואח"כ נמצאת הראשונה תמות
notes.he: משום דהויא אבודה בשעת כפרה וכן המפריש מעות לחטאתו ואבדו והקריב חטאת אחר' תחתיה:
notes.en: One who designates a sin offering and it was lost, and he sacrificed another in its place, and afterward the first was found, it shall die: because it is lost at the time of atonement. And likewise one who designates money for his sin offering and it was lost, and he sacrificed another sin offering in its place,

messages.text: In the case of one who designates money for purchase of his sin offering, and the money was lost, and he designated an animal as a sin offering in its stead, and he sacrificed it, and thereafter, the money was found, it is prohibited to derive benefit from the money, as the money attains the halakhic status of the sin offering that was to be purchased with it, and that sin offering would be left to die because the owner achieved atonement with another animal. Therefore, he must take the money and cast it into the Dead Sea, from where it cannot be recovered.

notes.he: כל היכא דאי הוה חטאת הוה מתה מעות נמי אזיל לים המלח:
notes.en: He must take it to the Dead Sea: wherever a sin offering would die, money too goes to the Dead Sea.

notes.dh: ואח"כ נמצאו לאחר כפרה ילכו לים המלח
notes.he: היינו במקום מיתה:
notes.en: and afterward, after atonement, it was found: it shall go to the Dead Sea, that is, in place of dying.

messages.text: In the case of one who designates money for purchase of his sin offering, and the money was lost, and he designated other money in its stead, and he did not manage to purchase a sin offering with that money before the original money was found, he should bring a sin offering from a combination of this original money and that money designated in its stead, and the remainder shall be allocated for communal gift offerings.

notes.he: יערבו יחד דכיון דמתרוייהו מייתי לא הוו חטאת שכיפרו בעליה באחרת אבל אי הוה מייתו מחד מינייהו מידחו אחריני דהוו להו דמי חטאת שכיפרו בעלים באחרת אבל כי מייתי מאלו ומאלו ליכא חטאת שכפרו בעלים והוי כשאר מותר חטאת דאזיל לנדבה:
notes.en: From this and from that: they combine them together. Since he brings from both of them, they are not [the money of] a sin offering whose owner achieved atonement with another. But were he to bring from one of them, the other would be rejected, for it would be the money of a sin offering whose owner achieved atonement with another. When he brings from this and from that, there is no sin offering whose owner achieved atonement, and it is like any other surplus of a sin offering, which goes to gift offerings.

notes.dh: אבל המפריש מעות לחטאתו ונאבדו והפריש מעות אחרים תחתיהם ולא הספיק כו'
notes.he: יביא מאלו ומאלו חטאת ששניהם ראויין ליקח מהן שהראשונה לא נאבדו אלא בשעת הפרשה בלבד והשאר המותר מאלו ומאלו יפלו לנדבה:
notes.en: But one who designates money for his sin offering and it was lost, and he designated other money in its place and did not manage, etc.: he brings a sin offering from this and from that, for both are fit to buy from, since the first was lost only at the time of designation; and the remainder, the surplus of this and of that, goes to gift offerings.

messages.text: In the case of one who designates money for purchase of his sin offering, and the money was lost, and he designated an animal as a sin offering in its stead, and he did not manage to sacrifice the animal before the money was found, and the animal that he designated as a sin offering is blemished, the animal shall be sold; and he brings a sin offering from a combination of this original money and that money received for the sale of the blemished animal, and the remainder shall be allocated for communal gift offerings.

notes.he: אבל אם היתה תמימה תיקרב היא והמעות ילכו לים המלח הואיל וכיפרו הבעלים באחרת. וכל הנך אליבא דרבי:
notes.en: It shall be sold, and he brings from this and from that, etc.: but if it was unblemished, it is sacrificed and the money goes to the Dead Sea, since the owner achieved atonement with another. And all these follow Rabbi.

notes.he: וכן המפריש מעות לחטאתו ואבדו והפריש חטאת תחתיה ולא הספיק להקריבה עד שנמצאו המעות והרי חטאת בעל מום תמכר ודינו כמעות דלעיל וכן לא שנא הפריש המעות תחילה ואח"כ חטאת ונמצאת בעל מום או הפריש חטאת תחילה ואח"כ מעות או הפריש חטאת ואח"כ חטאת ושניהם בעל מום דהוו קדושת דמים דינן אחד הוא:
notes.en: And likewise one who designates money for his sin offering and it was lost, and he designated a sin offering in its place and did not manage to sacrifice it before the money was found, and the sin offering is blemished: it is sold, and its law is like the money above. And likewise there is no difference whether he designated money first and afterward a sin offering that was found blemished, or he designated a sin offering first and afterward money, or he designated a sin offering and afterward a sin offering and both are blemished: since they have sanctity of value, their law is one.

messages.text: In the case of one who designates a sin offering and the animal was lost, and he designated money in its stead, and he did not manage to purchase a sin offering with that money before his sin offering was found, and the animal is blemished, the animal shall be sold; and he brings a sin offering from a combination of this money that he designated and that money received for the sale of the blemished animal, and the remainder shall be allocated for communal gift offerings.

In the case of one who designates his sin offering and the animal was lost, and he designated another animal in its stead, and he did not manage to sacrifice the sin offering before the first sin offering was found, and both of the animals are blemished, the animals shall be sold; and he brings a sin offering from a third animal that he buys with a combination of the money from the sale of this animal and from the sale of that animal, and the remainder shall be allocated for communal gift offerings.

In the case of one who designates his sin offering and the animal was lost, and he designated another animal in its stead, and he did not manage to sacrifice the sin offering before the first sin offering was found, and both of the animals are unblemished and fit for sacrifice:
One of them shall be sacrificed as a sin offering and the other shall be left to die; this is the statement of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi.
A sin offering is not left to die unless it was found after its owner achieved atonement; and the money is not taken to the Dead Sea unless it was found after its owner achieved atonement.

notes.he: ואפילו נתכפר באחת מן הצבורין לאחר שנמצא האבוד הואיל וקודם כפרה נמצא:
notes.en: And the money does not go to the Dead Sea: even if he achieved atonement with one of the sums after the lost one was found, since it was found before atonement.

notes.he: מחלוקת רבי ורבנן דר' אית ליה אבודה בשעת הפרשה מתה ורבנן סברי אין מתה אלא אבודה בשעת כפרה והוא הדין למעות:
notes.en: One who designates a sin offering and it was lost, etc.: a dispute of Rabbi and the Rabbis. Rabbi holds that one lost at the time of designation dies, and the Rabbis hold it dies only [if] lost at the time of atonement; and the same is true of money.

messages.text: In the case of one who designates a sin offering and the animal is blemished, he sells the animal and must bring another sin offering with the money received in its sale.

If the second animal is sacrificed before the first is slaughtered for non-sacred consumption, the first animal shall be left to die. Although it was sold and rendered non-sacred, its status is now that of a sin offering whose owner already achieved atonement with another animal.

notes.dh: אם קרבה שניה עד שלא נשחטה
notes.he: הראשונה בבית לוקח לאכילת חולין תמות אף ע"פ שהיא חולין דחטאת שכיפרו הבעלים היא:
notes.en: If the second was sacrificed before it was slaughtered: [i.e.,] before the first was slaughtered in the buyer’s house to be eaten as non-sacred meat, it shall die, even though it is non-sacred, for it is a sin offering whose owner achieved atonement.

notes.he: המפריש חטאת ובשעת שחיטה נמצאת שהיא בעל מום מוכרה והיא חולין ויביא בדמיה אחרת ר' אלעזר ב"ר שמעון אומר כו'. מפרש טעמא בסיפא דפירקין משום דפסולי המוקדשין אלימי למיתפס פדיונן:
notes.en: One who designates a sin offering, and at the time of slaughter it is found to be blemished: he sells it, and it is non-sacred, and he brings another with its money. Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon says, etc. The reason is explained at the end of our chapter: because disqualified consecrated animals are potent enough to impart their status to their redemption.

messages.caption: The mishna’s cases: a sin offering or its money lost, replaced, and then found.

messages.text: Gemara

The reason the animal is left to die is that he sacrificed another animal in its stead; but if he did not sacrifice another in its stead, and instead merely designated it, then the original sin offering is left to graze. In accordance with whose opinion is this statement?
