It is in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis, who say that if a sin offering was lost at the time when another animal was designated in its stead, the original sin offering is left to graze.
messages.quote: and he designated another in its stead and sacrificed it, and thereafter the first animal was found

notes.he: כגון הנך מעות דנמצאו קודם כפרה ואזלו לים המלח אי לא מצי מייתי מאלו ומאלו:
notes.en: Gemara. Lost at the time of designation: such as this money, which was found before atonement and goes to the Dead Sea if he could not bring from this and from that.

messages.text: But now say the latter clause of the mishna: In the case of one who designates money for purchase of his sin offering, and the money was lost, and he designated other money in its stead, he should bring a sin offering from a combination of this original money and that money designated in its stead, and the remainder shall be allocated for communal gift offerings.
messages.quote: he should bring a sin offering from a combination of this original money and that money designated in its stead

notes.he: דליכא למימר דנתכפרו בעלים באחרת:
notes.en: The reason is “from this and from that”: for one cannot say that the owner achieved atonement with another.

messages.text: One may infer that the reason that the remainder is allocated for communal gift offerings is that he brings a sin offering from a combination of this original money and that money designated in its stead; but if the owner brought a sin offering from one of the two sums of money, he must take the other sum of money and cast it into the Dead Sea. If so, we arrive at the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi, who said: A sin offering that was lost at the time when another animal was designated in its stead is left to die.

notes.he: חטאת מאחת מן הציבורין השני ילך לים המלח ואע"ג דנמצא קודם כפרה ולא היה אבוד אלא בשעת הפרשה:
notes.en: But if he brought: a sin offering from one of the sums, the second goes to the Dead Sea, even though it was found before atonement and was lost only at the time of designation.

notes.he: טעמא משום דיש מותר מאלו ומאלו משום הכי יפלו לנדבה הא הביא מאלו משאינן אבודין ולא נשתייר מהן כלום ולא הביא מאלו מן האבודין ילכו האבודין לים המלח אע"ג דלא הי' אבודה אלא בשעת הפרשה ולא בשעת כפרה אתיא לרבי דאמר אבודה בשעת הפרשה מתה רישא רבנן וסיפא רבי:
notes.en: The reason is that there is a remainder from this and from that; that is why it goes to gift offerings. But if he brought from these, which were not lost, and nothing of them remained, and did not bring from these, the lost ones, the lost ones go to the Dead Sea, even though it was lost only at the time of designation and not at the time of atonement. This accords with Rabbi, who said one lost at the time of designation dies. The first clause is the Rabbis, and the latter clause is Rabbi.

messages.text: Can it be that the first clause of the mishna is in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis, while the latter clause is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi?
This works out well according to Rav Huna, as Rav Huna said that Rav said:

notes.he: לקמן:
notes.en: This works out well according to Rav Huna, who said: below [on 23a].

notes.he: לקמן בהא שמעתא הכל מודין. בין רבי ובין רבנן כשנמצאת האבודה והרי שתיהן עומדות תמימין שאם משך אחת מהן מדעתו שלא נמלך איזו יקריב אלא הקריב מדעתו אחת שהשניה מתה לדברי הכל ה"נ סיפא דקא דייקינן הא הביא מאלו ולא הביא מאלו אמאי ילכו לים המלח הנך דנשתיירו משום דמשך אחת מהן מהלין מעות מדעתו והקריבן הלכך ילכו האחרים לים המלח לדברי הכל ומיתוקמא רישא וסיפא כרבנן:
notes.en: This works out well according to Rav Huna, who said: below, in this very discussion. [A footnote in the printed edition says: up to here belongs to the previous amud; that is, what follows explains Rav Huna’s statement on 23a.] All concede, both Rabbi and the Rabbis, that when the lost one is found and both stand unblemished, if he drew one of them on his own, that is, he did not consult about which to sacrifice but sacrificed one on his own, the second dies according to all. So too in the latter clause, from which we inferred “but if he brought from this and not from that,” why do [the others] go to the Dead Sea? Because he drew one of these sums of money on his own and sacrificed them; therefore the others go to the Dead Sea according to all. And so both the first clause and the latter clause are established according to the Rabbis.

messages.text: Rav Huna’s statement in the name of Rav continues on 23a.
